title: Stalk complex of termwise tensor pullback
statement: Let X and Y be ringed spaces, f:X→Y continuous, and α:f⁻¹ OY→OX a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings. Let K be a Z-indexed cochain complex of OY-modules and P a Z-indexed cochain complex of OX-modules. For every i assume an isomorphism e_i:P^i≅changeOfRings α (inverseImageModule f OY K^i) [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module]. Assume the square P.d(i,j) followed by e_j equals e_i followed by changeOfRingsHom α applied to inverseImageModuleMap of K.d(i,j), for all i,j. For every x∈X there exists a unital ring homomorphism ρ:OY_(f x)→OX_x and an isomorphism of OX_x-module cochain complexes (ModuleCat.extendScalars ρ applied termwise to K_(f x))≅P_x. Stalk complexes use [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. The canonical choice of ρ is the inverse-image ring-stalk isomorphism followed by α_x; the existential statement suffices and does not assert uniqueness. No acyclicity, flatness, or boundedness assumption is present.

source.place: Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules; degreewise naturality as used in Cohomology Tag 06YC; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0098

proof.text: Use the natural inverse-image stalk isomorphisms for rings and abelian groups to identify (f⁻¹ OY)_x with OY_(f x) and the inverse-image module stalks with the original module stalks. Transport the abelian-group comparison to a linear comparison over the ring-stalk identification: represent the scalar and module element on a common neighborhood and use the unit germ formula and semilinearity of the inverse-image unit. The chosen inverse-image action has that property by exists_inverseImageModuleInstances. Define ρ by composing the inverse ring-stalk comparison with α_x.

Apply stalkChangeOfRingsIso degreewise to the inverse-image modules. Combine it with the preceding linear comparison, transporting scalars through the ring-stalk isomorphism. This gives OX_x-linear isomorphisms from extension of scalars of K_(f x)^i to the changed inverse-image stalks. Naturality of both comparisons on the module differentials identifies the differentials with ModuleCat.extendScalars ρ.map applied to the original stalk differentials.

Take stalks of the termwise isomorphisms e_i using the module stalk functor, and compose with their inverses to obtain maps into P_x. Apply the stalk functor to the assumed differential squares; composition preservation and the previous naturality give the chain-map squares. The inverse maps satisfy these squares as well, giving an isomorphism of complexes. No claim of K-flatness is used in this comparison.

theorem exists_tensorPullback_stalk_complex_iso
    (X Y : RingedSpace.{u}) (f : X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier)
    (α : TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f Y.sheaf ⟶ X.sheaf)
    (K : CochainComplex (RingedSpace.Modules Y) ℤ)
    (P : CochainComplex (RingedSpace.Modules X) ℤ)
    (e : ∀ i : ℤ, P.X i ≅
      SheafOfModules.changeOfRings.{u, u, u} α
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule f Y.sheaf (K.X i)))
    (he : ∀ i j : ℤ, P.d i j ≫ (e j).hom =
      (e i).hom ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom.{u, u, u} α
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModule f Y.sheaf (K.X i))
        (TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageModuleMap f Y.sheaf (K.X i) (K.d i j)))
    (x : X) :
    ∃ ρ : Y.presheaf.stalk (f x) →+* X.presheaf.stalk x,
      Nonempty
        ((((ModuleCat.extendScalars ρ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
          (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor Y (f x)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K)) ≅
        (((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X x).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P))
